title: Lena and the Alibi
premise: Ansel Sterling, the reclusive archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years solving deaths the police dismissed, hiding behind her institutional invisibility. When missing parishioner Maren Voss's diary keeps receiving entries after her disappearance, Ansel realizes Maren is alive and hiding—and that the diary implicates Dean Corvus Hale, the cathedral's beloved leader, in a death he staged as an accident. As the trial of Hale's scapegoat approaches, Ansel must find the 'dead' witness before Hale silences her for good. In the crypt beneath the locked door, Ansel confronts Hale, exposes him with the diary's final entry, and chooses truth over the safety invisibility once bought her.
about_author: Freya Vane is the pen name of a former parish administrator who spent a decade among vestry minutes, burial registers, and things no one wanted written down. She writes mysteries about quiet people who notice too much.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She catalogs the cathedral archives, noting the crypt key that hasn't turned in eleven years, and quietly closes out her third unofficial investigation—a fall from the bell tower ruled accidental. Emotional beat: the comfort of being unseen, and its first faint crack.

chapters.title: A Diary That Keeps Writing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Donated to the archive among Maren Voss's effects, the diary contains entries dated after her disappearance—handwriting Ansel verifies as genuine. The last entry names someone inside the cathedral. Emotional beat: dread blooming in a place that should feel safe.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with flashback. She reviews her three solved cases: all connected to the same winter, all witnesses now dead or gone. She realizes Maren may be the fourth thread. Emotional beat: the pattern she can no longer unsee.

chapters.title: Dean Hale's Warm Welcome
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins—Hale's chapters show his public charm and private calculation. He praises Ansel's discretion and hints the archive should be 'thinned.' Emotional beat: flattery that feels like a leash.

chapters.title: The Scapegoat
chapters.summary: Detective Ilsa Reyes POV. The trial of Tom Bracken, accused in one of the 'accidents,' is three weeks away; Reyes privately doubts the case but has no evidence. She notices Ansel's anonymous letters from years past. Emotional beat: an investigator's itch she can't scratch.

chapters.title: Entries in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Forensic comparison shows the post-disappearance entries were written by Maren herself—alive, and writing to someone she expected to find the diary. A meeting is arranged at the boathouse. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Is Empty
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She arrives to find signs of hurried departure and a fresh cigarette brand Hale smokes. Someone else decoded the diary's location. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she has become the hunted.

chapters.title: What the Vestry Knew
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Buried in minutes and ledgers, she reconstructs the embezzlement scheme: restoration funds funneled through a shell charity, with Maren as bookkeeper and the three 'accidents' as its cleanup crew. Emotional beat: corruption wearing vestments.

chapters.title: Hale's Version of Mercy
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. He offers Ansel a funded sabbatical, then gently mentions her late brother and how grief makes people imagine patterns. Emotional beat: menace dressed as kindness; power corrupting through generosity.

chapters.title: Reyes Comes to the Archive
chapters.summary: Reyes POV. She confronts Ansel about the old letters; Ansel shares just enough—the diary dates—to make an ally without exposing Maren. Emotional beat: two cautious women deciding to trust across institutional lines.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Following the diary's coded references to a coastal convent, she finds proof Maren took refuge there under a new name—and that a letter confirming it was intercepted. Emotional beat: the witness lives; the clock is merciless.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Under Lock
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback-heavy. The crypt's history: what Hale sealed away after his predecessor's sudden death, and why the key matters. Emotional beat: the cathedral itself revealed as an accomplice.

chapters.title: Bracken Refuses to Talk
chapters.summary: Reyes POV. In holding, Bracken hints he's protecting someone and fears for his daughter. Reyes realizes the trial is a trap designed to close the case forever. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized against the innocent.

chapters.title: A Fire in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A small fire nearly destroys the archive section holding her evidence; she saves the diary by instinct and loses everything else. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve—she memorizes what burns.

chapters.title: The Convent Road
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Traveling under pretext of archival research, she reaches the convent and meets Mother Cecilia, who neither confirms nor denies—but leaves a door unlocked. Emotional beat: solidarity passed like a candle flame.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She tells her story: the ledgers, the night she saw the fourth accident happen, the faked drowning arranged by a man who claimed it was mercy. She will testify only if Bracken's daughter is protected. Emotional beat: survival's price, finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Intercepted Letter
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. He learns the convent contact failed and prepares his endgame: discredit Ansel as unstable, move the trial up, and open the crypt one last time to remove what's buried there. Emotional beat: a powerful man discovering fear.

chapters.title: Trial Eve
chapters.summary: Split POV. Reyes secures protective custody for Bracken's daughter; Ansel sends Maren's sworn statement to the court—but Hale files a motion challenging its authenticity, and Ansel is subpoenaed. Emotional beat: every piece on the board, trembling.

chapters.title: The Crypt Opens
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Summoned at night to authenticate documents, she realizes the summons is forged—and that Hale is below, opening the crypt to destroy his predecessor's records and the body that proves the first 'accident' was murder. Emotional beat: terror and clarity arriving together.

chapters.title: What Was Buried
chapters.summary: Climax, Ansel's POV. Confrontation in the crypt: Hale's confession, half-threat and half-eulogy, as Reyes arrives with the recording Ansel deliberately triggered. Hale tries to seal them in; the eleventh-year lock mechanism fails him. Emotional beat: truth dragged into the light at the cost of near-death.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Reyes POV. The trial collapses into Hale's indictment; Maren testifies, Bracken walks free, and the cathedral's chapter resigns in disgrace. Ansel declines credit, but Reyes insists on putting her name in the file. Emotional beat: justice that costs what it costs.

chapters.title: The Unlocked Door
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. Months later, the crypt is a public memorial; Ansel remains archivist, but no longer invisible—she teaches a young volunteer to read the ledgers. Final line echoes the diary's last entry. Emotional beat: survival redeemed; loyalty and truth finally aligned.
